Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: A
Q2: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: All three failures concern files that exist only on PR #7249's head. GitHub shows `ai/issue-7228` open at `63df62d6d676`, and this checkout of the default branch has no `scripts/pr_dependency.py`. That rules out option C. Fixing on the PR head is what the triage asked for, and the head branch is the only place these files exist. One caveat: `scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh` reads `Target branch:` / `Integration branch:` only from the issue body (`get_issue_body`, line 67). `CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING_ENABLED` defaults to `false` in `plan.yml` and `implement.yml`, and the checkout for this run was the default branch. So this answer alone does not move planning onto `ai/issue-7228`. See the routing safeguard under Q2's plan.
Q2: The test exists to cover the issue-specific fail-closed path. Changing the fixture to a run with no tracking issue (or standalone recovery only) reaches that path, and the identity guard at `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18805-18815` stays as it is. Option B would stop testing the issue-specific path. Option C makes the change bigger than this CI repair needs.

EXECUTION PLAN:
Q1 (routing safeguard; the decision is a letter, but this is how it gets executed):
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh (reads branch lines from the issue body only)
    - .github/workflows/plan.yml, .github/workflows/implement.yml (`CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING_ENABLED` defaults to `false`)
    - Unblock judge #7032 (agents.md): a reissue of a standalone, non-security CI-failure issue whose PR is open gets a `- Integration branch:` line with the PR head ref.
  steps:
    - Planner: check the planning checkout before writing a plan. If `scripts/pr_dependency.py` is missing, or the branch is not `ai/issue-7228`, do not plan against the default branch. Emit `BLOCKED: fix must land on PR #7249 head branch ai/issue-7228; planning checkout lacks scripts/pr_dependency.py`. The unblock judge then reissues the issue with an `Integration branch: ai/issue-7228` line.
    - If the checkout is `ai/issue-7228`, plan three edits:
      (a) Add a `scripts/pr_dependency.py` entry to `docs/INVENTORY.md`, next to the related entries around lines 303-307.
      (b) In `tests/test_pr_dependency.py::test_gates_are_wired_with_trusted_isolated_copies` (around line 187), stop requiring `pr_dependency.py` to be the last case alternative. Assert instead that the helper is one of the alternatives copied into the trusted host-Python directory in `.github/workflows/clarify.yml:274-276`.
      (c) Do the Q2 fix.
    - Do not change any workflow, script or prompt. Only `docs/INVENTORY.md` and the two test files are in scope.
  reversibility: If PR #7249 merges first, or its own review/autofix loop fixes these failures, this issue becomes a no-op. It can then be closed as not planned.
Q2:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:5844-5848 (the assertion) and 1382-1386 (the fixture creates a tracking issue)
    - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18805-18815 (the earlier fail-closed identity check)
  steps:
    - On `ai/issue-7228`, run `python3 -m pytest tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py -k test_standalone_pr_dependency_fails_closed_without_identity_or_trust` to get the full traceback. The CI log shows only the test name.
    - If the run stops at the tracking-state identity guard, change this test's fixture so it has no open tracking issue (or runs standalone recovery only). Keep the issue-specific assertion as written.
    - If the traceback shows a different cause, fix the test or fixture for that cause. Do not change the poller's identity guard or its fail-closed behaviour.
  reversibility: Only the test changes. If a person wants the earlier-guard case covered too, it can be added later as a separate case, as in option C.
